title: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Fine quantum amendment Article 45
sections.summary: Clause 3 amends the Article 45(1)(e) fine from not less than $2,000 to not less than $10,000, unchanged since Independence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Clause 3 of the Bill amends the current fine quantum in Article 45(1)(e) of "not less than $2,000" to "not less than $10,000".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The current fine quantum of "not less than $2,000" has not been revised since Singapore's Independence.

sections.label: Inflation effect on $2,000
sections.summary: Taking inflation into account, $2,000 would amount to about $8,000 today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: First, if we were to take into account inflation over the years, $2,000 would amount to about $8,000 today.

sections.label: Disqualification extends to foreign courts
sections.summary: Clause 3 extends disqualification from conviction by a court beyond Singapore and Malaysia to any foreign court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Clause 3 also extends the disqualification due to conviction by a court of law beyond Singapore and Malaysia to any foreign court.

sections.label: Updated disqualification criteria
sections.summary: The fine quantum is revised to not less than $10,000, and disqualification criteria for CPA, PCMR members and presidential candidates are similarly updated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, what is proposed, as mentioned by the hon Minister, is to revise the fine quantum from "not less than $2,000" to "not less than $10,000".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As a consequence, it is proposed that the disqualification criteria for a member of CPA and PCMR, as well as a candidate standing for election as the President be similarly updated.

sections.label: Automatic disqualification five-year period
sections.summary: The automatic disqualification ceases after a five-year period under Article 45(2) of the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Even then, the automatic disqualification ceases after a five-year period, as provided for under Article 45(2) of the Constitution.

sections.label: Imprisonment under one year
sections.summary: If the sentence of imprisonment is less than one year, he is not automatically disqualified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If the sentence of imprisonment is less than one year, then he is not automatically disqualified.

sections.label: Punishments for convicted civil servants
sections.summary: Civil servants and uniformed officers convicted of crimes may be dismissed, reduced in rank or otherwise punished.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Civil servants and uniformed officers convicted of crimes may be dismissed, reduced in rank or otherwise punished, too.

sections.label: Standards for sitting MPs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether it is anomalous that the saluting officer is held to a higher standard, and suggests considering similar requirements for sitting MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Is it not anomalous that the saluting officer is held to a higher standard, as compared to us?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, we might want to consider if we want to impose similar requirements on sitting MPs.

sections.label: Raising disqualifying fine threshold
sections.summary: The Bill raises the threshold for a disqualifying Court fine from $2,000 to $10,000, and does not deal directly with sitting MPs' disqualification criteria or parity of standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To my mind, it is a simple updating exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill does not propose to deal directly with two other important matters: the disqualification criteria of sitting MPs and the parity of standards between sitting MPs and professionals, civil servants and uniformed officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This "second key", in my respectful view, appears to be weaker for MPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In essence, the current law of disqualifying a person once he has received a Court fine of at least $2,000 is being amended.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The threshold for a disqualifying Court fine is proposed to be raised to $10,000.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Bill to raise the threshold fines for disqualification from Parliament to $10,000, and suggests a possible future review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To summarise then, the Workers' Party supports the Bill to raise the threshold fines for disqualification from Parliament to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have also raised the suggestion of a possible future review on the issue of disqualifications based on fines to further examine if it is appropriate to either remove fines altogether or to look at further refinements.

sections.label: Article 45(e) disqualification
sections.summary: Article 45(e) states a person is not qualified to be an MP if convicted and sentenced to imprisonment of not less than one year or a fine of not less than $2,000 without a free pardon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Article 45(e) states that a person shall not be qualified to be an MPs if he has been convicted of an offence by a Court of law and sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not less than one year or a fine of not less than $2,000 and has not received a free pardon.

sections.label: Bar for MP disqualification
sections.summary: The speaker submits that the Constitution should disqualify a person from being an MP for offences relating to dishonesty, fraud, corruption, bribery or sexual misconduct, but not careless driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, it begs the question as to whether a momentary lapse of judgement whilst driving is the kind of reason that a person ought to be disqualified to serve as an MP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And I would humbly submit that we ought to set a bar in the Constitution that disqualifies a person from being an MP if that person is convicted of an offence that relates to dishonesty, fraud, corruption, bribery or, as Mr Murali Pillai has suggested, sexual misconduct, but not for careless driving.

sections.label: Disqualification criteria and dishonest conduct
sections.summary: The speaker says disqualification criteria show the state frowns on dishonest persons and urges the Government to signal the dishonest conduct to guard against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: These disqualification criteria suggest that the state frowns upon persons who have behaved dishonestly and are disqualified from holding positions where they act as fiduciary to either a charity or a company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I would urge the Government to do likewise – signal the type of dishonest conduct that we wish to guard against and not just by adjusting the quantum of the fine.

sections.label: Foreign court fine disqualification
sections.summary: An individual fined at least S$10,000 by a foreign court is disqualified if the offence would be punishable in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: An individual who has been fined by a foreign court the equivalent of at least S$10,000 will be disqualified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: However, it must be for an offence which would be punishable by a Court in Singapore if it had been committed locally.

sections.label: Bill updates disqualification criteria
sections.summary: The Bill aims to update disqualification criteria for Parliament, CPA and PCMR membership so Members remain persons of integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Bill aims to update the disqualification criteria for membership of Parliament and memberships of CPA and PCMR so that they continue to be relevant in ensuring that Members are persons with integrity and who adhere to high standards of conduct.

sections.label: Standards and four keys of democracy
sections.summary: The passage states democracy needs four keys: rules, party expectations, MPs' self-accountability, and the electorate as strongest safeguard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, the standards that each and every one of us hold ourselves to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And third, and most importantly, the standards which our public hold us to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In order for our democracy to function properly, we need all four keys.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We need the first key, the set of rules that balance the need for democratic participation with the standards that we expect from those aspiring for public office but, very critically, the other three keys – what political parties expect of the standards from their respective MPs or candidates; how our candidates and MPs hold ourselves accountable to the standards that we expect of ourselves as representatives of our people and our country; and, finally, the strongest safeguard against any degradation of the standards of this House must be our electorate who, ultimately, elect our people into this House.

sections.label: Second Reading voting results
sections.summary: The Second Reading of the Bill was carried with 87 Ayes, 0 Noes and 0 Abstentions, by at least two-thirds of Elected and Non-Constituency Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 87 "Ayes"; 0 "Noes"; 0 "Abstentions".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Second Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament.    .
